title: Atoms across a hair
hook: Atoms are small. But how many would it take to cross one hair?

knows: that things are made of atoms
that a micrometre is a thousandth of a millimetre and a nanometre a thousandth of a micrometre (or will accept it)
doesNotKnow: how big an atom is compared with everyday thin things

misconception: Atoms are 'really small' but only thousands of them would span something thin like a hair.
objective: The learner can explain that a hair is about 350,000 atoms wide, five and a half factors of ten, by counting tenfold zoom steps from the hair to single atoms.

claims.text: A human hair is about 70 micrometres wide (hairs range from roughly 17 to 180 micrometres).
claims.source: B. Ley, 'Diameter of a Human Hair', The Physics Factbook (ed. G. Elert, 1999), which collects published values of 17-181 µm; 70 µm is a commonly used typical value. The CM's 'Ley & Bartlett, J. Cosmet. Sci. 2008' citation could not be confirmed and was replaced; a fact-checker should confirm a primary measurement.

claims.text: An atom is about 0.2 nanometres across (atoms run roughly 0.1 to 0.5 nm).
claims.source: Twice the covalent radii in Cordero et al., Dalton Trans. (2008) 2832 (e.g. C 0.76 Å, O 0.66 Å, Si 1.11 Å) and twice the van der Waals radii in Bondi, J. Phys. Chem. 68 (1964) 441 (C 1.70 Å, O 1.52 Å) give about 0.13-0.34 nm for common atoms; heavy alkali atoms reach about 0.5 nm.

claims.text: About 350,000 atoms side by side span a 70 µm hair: 70,000 nm ÷ 0.2 nm, so atoms are hundreds of thousands of times smaller than a hair's width.
claims.source: 70 x 10^-6 m / 0.2 x 10^-9 m = 3.5 x 10^5; log10(3.5 x 10^5) = 5.54, 'about five and a half powers of ten' (node script). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): node: 70e-6/0.2e-9 = 350,000; log10 = 5.54. Matches Demo.tsx HAIR_UM 70, ATOM_NM 0.2 and reveal text.

claims.text: Windows 100 µm, 10 µm, 1 µm, 100 nm, 10 nm and 1 nm wide are 500,000, 50,000, 5,000, 500, 50 and 5 atom widths across.
claims.source: Window width / 0.2 nm: 100,000/0.2 = 500,000, and each zoom divides by 10.

claims.text: The hair fills 70% of the first 100 µm window, so it spans about 0.7 × 500,000 = 350,000 atoms.

recall.question: A plastic film is 100 micrometres thick. Roughly how many atoms (about 0.2 nm each) stacked up make that thickness?
recall.why: 100 µm is 100,000 nm, and 100,000 / 0.2 = 500,000: five and a bit factors of ten, like the hair.
